thread:
maya: quick heads-up — trying to onboard model xhal-13B. weights fetched from s3://redwood-models/xhal-13b/v1 and tokenizer v0.4. but getting some weird outputs in staging (hallucinations + tokenization strangely splitting emojis). anyone seen this combo before?
eli: can you paste the exact s3 path and the sha? also which tokenizer package/version did you pin?
maya: path: s3://redwood-models/xhal-13b/v1/weights.tar.gz sha256: f3a1c9d2... (pasted truncated). tokenizer wheel: tokenizr==0.4.2. running `redwoodctl model validate` shows a checksum warning.
sanjeev: re: checksum — CI's integrity job flagged that weights.tar.gz checksum != repo recorded value. CI output: `expected 9b2c..., actual f3a1...`. could be an upload retry corruption.
maya: hmm — I re-uploaded earlier today after a failed multipart. maybe the upload tool retried and left a partial artifact.
ops-bot: @maya noticed asset checksum mismatch for s3://redwood-models/xhal-13b/v1/weights.tar.gz. Opened ticket #INF-2345.
eli: if weights are corrupted, that could explain OOMs on load too — bad file layout can confuse mmap. Did you hit an OOM during serve or during load?
maya: during container init / model load on a 32GB GPU node — container crashed with OOM while allocating KV cache. stack snippet: ```
AllocationError: Failed to allocate 12143576 bytes
  at backend/gpu/memory_pool.c:line 412
  at loader/weights.c:line 78
```
rachel: separate note: tokenizer v0.4.2 had a BPE merge table bug where emojis like :rocket: were split into multiple unknown tokens. We patched v0.4.3 yesterday. If staging used 0.4.2, that could explain the odd hallucination alignment.
maya: good call — my env pinned 0.4.2 due to previous compatibility concerns. sanjeev, can you confirm if the dedicated onboarding CI used 0.4.3?
sanjeev: onboarding CI matrix shows tokenizr 0.4.3 for most flows, but model xhal entry in the manifest still lists 0.4.2 because it was added before the patch. manifest line: `models/xhal-13b/manifest.yaml: tokenizer: tokenizr==0.4.2`
eli: two issues then: corrupted weights upload + tokenizer mismatch. Priority is to prevent bad outputs in prod. Plan: 1) rollback any canary serving of xhal-13b (if enabled), 2) re-upload verified weights, 3) update manifest to 0.4.3 and run full validate, 4) add a checksum gate in the upload step. anyone disagree?
maya: +1. I'm taking point on re-upload. I'll run `aws s3 cp` with `--expected-size` and `sha256sum` locally before pushing.
ops-bot: @eli requested rollback: canary routes for model xhal-13b disabled.
eli: I'll open a tiny PR to bump manifest and add an automated checksum check in the onboarding pipeline. attaching draft: https://git.redwood/models/pull/412 (WIP)
sanjeev: quick safety: add a runtime fallback that rejects loads if weights checksum doesn't match manifest, rather than attempting partial mmap. That would avoid strange OOMs and make errors deterministic.
rachel: also add a tokenizer compatibility assert: `tokenizer.version == manifest.tokenizer` on startup and fail early with a clear error message. We should surface that in the Console under model validation errors.
maya: uploading verified weights now, running local validate. output from `redwoodctl model validate --path models/xhal-13b/v1`: ```
VALIDATION: FAIL
 - checksum mismatch: expected 9b2c..., got f3a1c9d2...
 - tokenizer mismatch: found tokenizr 0.4.2, manifest 0.4.3
```
maya: re-upload complete, new sha256: 9b2c4f88... re-ran validate -> PASS.
eli: thanks — once PR is up for manifest bump and checksum gate I'll review. tagging @eng-oncall in case any prod traffic slipped through. :eyes:
ci-bot: CI run triggered for models/pull/412. Tests: upload-integrity, tokenizer-compat, startup-smoke.
ops-bot: INF-2345 updated: weights re-uploaded and manifest updated, canary disabled, monitoring alert suppressed after rollout.
maya: tl;dr — root causes: corrupted upload + stale tokenizer pin. mitigations: stricter upload checks, runtime checksum/asserts, manifest hygiene. I'll follow up with a short runbook for onboarding checklist. :memo:
eli: perfect. quick follow-ups: 1) add a small e2e that loads model in a 16GB GPU sim to catch OOM patterns, 2) add a smoke eval to detect obvious tokenization regressions.
sanjeev: will add the checks to onboarding pipeline this afternoon.
rachel: thanks team — will add runbook item to docs and note in release notes. :sparkles:
